name: Yemen
summary_text: Yemen is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. The legal framework criminalises same-sex conduct (up to death under some interpretations of the Penal Code; 100 lashes/1 year otherwise), but Cairo 52 emphasises the operative mechanism: the erosion of the rule of law and the power of militias has facilitated a surge in attacks targeting transgender individuals — de facto criminalisation operating outside any judicial system. Houthi-controlled areas impose their own moral-policing regime; the south has its own militia authorities. For a visitor: no safe authority to appeal to anywhere in the country.

sources.title: Yemen | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 country review of Yemen: the erosion of the rule of law, the humanitarian crisis and militia influence have facilitated a surge in attacks on trans people; criminalisation operates through less formal channels - non-state actors and civilians acting outside the judicial system, with morality laws serving as justification for vigilante action; legal provisions apply only in government-controlled areas amid the ongoing conflict.

sources.title: Audacity in Adversity: LGBT Activism in the Middle East and North Africa | HRW
sources.claim_summary: HRW report (April 2018) 'Audacity in Adversity': LGBT activism in the Middle East and North Africa - includes Yemen's criminalisation and the annex of laws used to punish same-sex conduct and gender expression across MENA.

sources.title: World Report 2026: Yemen | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW World Report 2026, Yemen chapter: Yemen remains one of the world's worst humanitarian crises (19.5 million needing assistance); includes a Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity section documenting abuses amid the conflict and Houthi control.

sources.title: Yemen: Huthis must stop executions and release dozens facing LGBTI charges - Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International (Feb 2024): 'Yemen: Huthis must stop executions and release dozens facing LGBTI charges' - two Houthi courts sentenced 40+ people to death, flogging or prison: in Dhamar, nine sentenced to death (seven by stoning, two by crucifixion) and 23 to prison for 'homosexuality' and 'spreading immorality'; in Ibb, 13 students sentenced to death for 'spreading homosexuality' - 'gruesome public spectacles aimed at spreading fear'.

sources.title: GayLawNet®™ | Laws | Yemen | YE
sources.claim_summary: GayLawNet laws page for Yemen: Penal Code 1994 - Article 264 (male homosexuality): unmarried men 100 lashes or up to 1 year, married men death by stoning; Article 268 (female homosexuality): up to 3 years, or up to 7 under duress.

sources.title: No Place for Gays in Yemen | Inter Press Service
sources.claim_summary: IPS (Aug 2013) by Shuaib Almosawa: 'No Place for Gays in Yemen' - Husam, 19, who spent his childhood under semi-house arrest, tucks his long hair inside a hood to pass checkpoints in Sana'a - a portrait of daily concealment and fear.
